Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Financial Services Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. In order to ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone. We will pause momentarily to compile the Q&A roster. Once again, press star one to register for a question.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review Apex Financial Services's results for the Q3. With me this morning are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Risk Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Credit Officer; David Kim, Chief Technology Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Operating Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Marketing Officer; and Jennifer Brooks, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Financial Services delivered record results in the Q3, exceeding all previous benchmarks and solidifying our position as a leader in the financial services industry.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on sustaining strong revenue growth, driving operational efficiency, managing risk effectively, investing in technology and innovation, enhancing customer experience, strengthening our brand reputation, promoting a diverse and inclusive culture, and delivering superior returns to our shareholders.

These priorities underpinned our standout performance across key areas, including overall company results, net interest margin dynamics, non-interest income resilience, revenue diversification efforts, credit loss provisions, deposit cost management, efficiency improvements, and capital returns. Sarah will dive into these in detail momentarily, but suffice it to say, we executed exceptionally well amid a complex macro backdrop.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning. Apex Financial Services reported net income of $3.8 billion for the Q3, or $2.05 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 11%, driven by growth in our loan portfolio and improved net interest margin. Non-interest income was robust, totaling around $4.8 billion and up 5% year-over-year, reflecting strong performance in our investment banking and wealth management businesses. We are generating strong returns on equity and are committed to delivering value to our shareholders.

Let me kick off our discussion with the overall company performance highlights, which underscore the resilience and strategic execution that continue to drive value for our shareholders. In a quarter marked by persistent macroeconomic headwinds—including the Federal Reserve's steady fed funds rate at 5.25-5.50%, lingering inflation pressures at 2.5% CPI, and geopolitical tensions impacting global trade—Apex delivered robust results. We reported record quarterly revenues of $16.2 billion, up 9% year-over-year and 3% quarter-over-quarter, fueled by net interest income expansion and diversified non-interest revenue streams. Net income attributable to common shareholders came in at $3.8 billion, a 12% YoY increase, translating to diluted EPS of $2.05—beating our consensus estimate of $1.98 and marking our 10th consecutive quarter of double-digit earnings growth.

Our balance sheet strength forms the bedrock of this performance. Total assets grew 6% YoY to $1.35 trillion, supported by disciplined loan portfolio expansion of 5.2% to $850 billion. Commercial and industrial loans, our highest-yielding segment, surged 8% YoY, driven by demand from middle-market clients in resilient sectors like technology and healthcare. Consumer loans grew a more modest 3%, reflecting cautious underwriting amid elevated 30-year mortgage rates near 6.8%. Credit quality remains pristine: the net charge-off rate ticked down to 28 basis points from 32 bps in Q3 2023, well below the industry average of 65 bps per FDIC data. Non-performing loans stood at just 0.85% of total loans, and our allowance for credit losses coverage ratio improved to 1.45%, positioning us conservatively for any softening in commercial real estate exposure, which we monitor closely given office vacancy rates exceeding 20% in major U.S. metros.

Deposits expanded 7.5% YoY to $1.05 trillion, with low-cost core deposits—checking and savings—comprising 68% of the mix, up from 65% a year ago. This growth outpaced peers like JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America. Our deposit cost of funds rose modestly to 2.1% from 1.8% YoY, but strategic pricing initiatives helped retain sticky balances. Liquidity is fortress-like, with our loan-to-deposit ratio at 81% and LCR at 125%.

Net interest income hit a quarterly record of $11.4 billion, up 11% YoY, as our NIM expanded 25 basis points to 3.55%. Non-interest income rose 5% YoY to $4.8 billion, or 30% of total revenue. Wealth and asset management fees jumped 15% to $1.2 billion, propelled by $45 billion in net new AUM totaling $650 billion. Investment banking fees increased 10% to $850 million.

Expense discipline improved our efficiency ratio to 52% from 55% YoY. Segmentally, Consumer Banking delivered 10% revenue growth to $6.5 billion; Commercial Banking grew 12% to $5.2 billion; Wealth & Investment Management up 8% to $4.5 billion. Regionally, U.S. operations grew 10%, Europe rebounded 7%, and Asia-Pacific surged 20% YoY to $1.2 billion. ROE expanded to 13.2%, tangible book value per share rose 8% to $52.40.

Building on that strong foundation, let's provide a detailed walkthrough of our net interest margin performance, including the key drivers behind the changes. Our disciplined asset-liability management continues to deliver resilient results in this high-rate, inverted yield curve environment.

Q3 NIM expanded 7 basis points quarter-over-quarter to 3.45%, and 25 basis points year-over-year from 3.20%. This marks our third consecutive quarter of NIM expansion, with trailing four-quarter NIM at 3.38%. Excluding our strategic securities portfolio repositioning—where we sold $2.5 billion of lower-yielding agency MBS—core NIM would be 3.52%. Interest income grew 12% YoY to $4.2 billion, while interest expense rose 18% to $2.1 billion.

Asset yields rose 25 basis points to 5.20%, fueled by 65% floating-rate loans linked to SOFR or Prime. Commercial loan yields expanded 35 basis points to 6.15%, with C&I up 10% YoY. Consumer yields steady at 4.85%, securities up 15 bps to 3.80%. Funding costs increased 40 basis points to 2.10%, with deposit beta at 45%—below industry 55%. Non-interest-bearing DDA grew 5% to $45 billion, 25% of deposits.

Regionally, Southeast U.S. NIM expanded 40 bps to 3.65%; Texas compressed to 3.25% due to competition. We've executed $5 billion in SOFR swaps to hedge fixed-rate loans and launched tiered high-yield savings via our digital platform, attracting $1.2 billion inflows. We expect Q4 NIM at 3.45-3.50%, with tailwinds from loan growth in higher-yielding segments.

Next, turning to the impact of market conditions on our non-interest income, which totaled $2.8 billion for the quarter, up 14% year-over-year and 8% quarter-over-quarter. This resilience underscores our diversified fee-based revenue streams amid a choppy macro environment with persistent inflation, Fed funds at 5.25-5.50%, VIX averaging 22, and slowdown in global M&A.

Investment banking fees contributed $850 million, or 30%. M&A advisory dipped 7% to $450 million due to 22% YoY volume decline and regulatory scrutiny, but debt underwriting steady at $250 million on IG spread tightening to 110 bps, and equity underwriting up 35% to $150 million from AI IPOs like a $4.5 billion generative AI fintech offering.

Trading revenues were a bright spot at $650 million, up 28% YoY, or 23% of total. Volatility drove equities volumes up 42% on S&P swings, fixed income gained $120 million from Treasury futures as 10-year yields hit 4.35%, FX/commodities up 15% on geopolitics spiking Brent to $85/barrel. Our trading VAR averaged $45 million daily, 10% below peers, via AI-driven stress testing.

Asset and wealth management fees hit $750 million, up 18%, with AUM at $1.2 trillion on $45 billion net inflows. Equity tailwinds, private markets up 25%. Americas strong at 65% AUM, Europe lagged on MiFID II. Card and payments $450 million, up 9%, with 7% volume growth and 45% digital wallet penetration via Apex Pay super-app processing $120 billion GPV.

North America drove 55% growth, EMEA flat, APAC up 25% to $450 million on RMB internationalization and $10 billion JV. Strategically, our $500 million Apex Alpha platform boosted trading alpha 15 bps, targeting 20% margins by 2026. We see 10-12% growth in Q4 assuming VIX to 18, with our 45% fee mix defensive.

On revenue diversification initiatives and their impact, we've reduced NII reliance to 58% of $14.2 billion quarterly revenue, with non-interest at 42% or $5.95 billion, up from 28% three years ago. This drove 12% YoY total revenue growth, outpacing industry 8%.

Wealth management AUM grew 18% to $1.8 trillion on $45 billion inflows, fees up 22% to $1.2 billion at 65 bps. AI-powered GlobalWealth Advisor boosted cross-sell 15%. Payments and cards $2.1 billion, up 24%, via Shopify/Stripe embeds processing 2.5 billion transactions at $0.84 avg revenue. IB fees $1.1 billion up 15%, trading $650 million up 10%. Bancassurance $450 million up 19%, green bonds $15 billion YTD at $180 million fees.

This mix lifted pre-tax margin 250 bps to 32%, ROTE to 14.2%. We're allocating $1.2 billion capex to cloud migration, gen-AI fraud detection cutting losses 18%, open banking APIs.

Now, our provision for credit losses came in at $450 million for Q3, up 15% quarter-over-quarter but flat YoY at 45 bps of average loans. This reflects disciplined CECL amid resilient consumers offset by commercial stress.

Macro overlay drove 60% or $270 million: baseline GDP 1.8% 2025, adverse recession at 20% weight. Consumer (55% of $250 billion book) released $50 million, delinquencies to 1.8%; C&I built $110 million on office CRE PDs to 2.5%, energy $40 million. Charge-offs $320 million or 32 bps.

CECL uses PD x LGD x EAD with ML enhancements, AUC 0.89, downturn LGD 55%, macro fan chart. CECL 2.0 adds real-time climate APIs. We've trimmed CRE $2 billion, allowance $4.2 billion or 1.4%. Q4 PCL $400-500 million.

Deposit costs averaged 2.85% in Q3, up 65 bps QoQ, with deposits 78% of funding, LDR 92%. Non-interest-bearing at 0.05% (28%), interest-bearing 2.45%, CDs 4.12%. Beta 42%, in line with peers.

Competition intense from JPM CDs at 4.75%, fintechs like Ally 4.20%, MMFs 5.25% drawing $1.2 trillion. Outflows $2.8 billion, but growth 4% annualized better than industry. Initiatives: relationship pricing to 3.25%, Deposit Boost app onboarding 45,000 accounts, BaaS with Chime, FHLB prepays. Q4 costs ~3.00%, NIM 3.45-3.55%.

Our efficiency ratio improved to 57.2%, down 410 bps YoY and 120 bps QoQ, YTD 58.1% toward 57-58% guidance, ahead of peers at 60.8%. Expenses $2.45 billion up 2%, revenue $4.28 billion up 8%. Retail 54%, Commercial 56%, Wealth 52%. U.S. 56.5%, Europe 59%, APAC 55%.

UniEfficient 2025: $450 million YTD on Temenos cloud (75% complete), AI fraud, RPA 60% back-office. GenAI pilots for 200 bps gains. Target mid-50s by 2025, $700 million savings.

Finally, on capital returns: target CET1 11.5-12.5%, now 11.8%. Dividend to $1.23/share quarterly, annual $4.92 at 40-45% payout. YTD repurchases $8.2 billion, 4.1% shares. New $15 billion authorization, $22-25 billion 2024 returns. Balanced 60/40, AI optimization freed $1.4 billion.

Thank you. I'll now hand over to Michael.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring commercial real estate pressures, deposit beta escalation, cybersecurity threats, and regulatory changes like Basel III Endgame. We are implementing enhanced controls and monitoring to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile.

Lisa Patel:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains excellent with non-performing loans at 0.85% and net charge-offs at 28 basis points. We are actively managing our loan portfolio and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment.

David Kim:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are leveraging technology to enhance customer experience, improve efficiency, and drive innovation. Our investments in AI-driven platforms and cloud-native infrastructure are yielding significant results, including fraud reduction and real-time analytics.

Elena Vasquez:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include streamlining our processes, optimizing our infrastructure, and leveraging data analytics to improve decision-making.

Robert Kline:
Thank you. From a marketing perspective, we are focused on strengthening our brand reputation and enhancing customer engagement. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly successful in driving customer acquisition and retention through digital channels and personalized offerings.

Jennifer Brooks:
Good morning. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of compliance and ethical conduct. We are continuously strengthening our compliance programs and working closely with regulators to ensure we are meeting all applicable requirements.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder to ask a question, please press star one. Our first question comes from John Doe with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

John Doe:
Good morning. Could you please provide more detail on revenue diversification initiatives and impact?

Johnathan Hale:
Good morning, John. Absolutely, our diversification has been transformative, reducing NII to 58% of revenue while non-interest income hit 42% or $5.95 billion. Wealth AUM up 18% to $1.8 trillion with fees up 22%, payments surging 24% on embedded finance, IB fees 15% higher, plus bancassurance and green bonds. This boosted margins 250 bps and buffered stress scenarios, with $1.2 billion capex fueling further growth. Happy to elaborate offline.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jane Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jane Smith:
What is your outlook for NIM?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks, Jane. Q4 NIM should hold 3.45-3.50%, supported by asset sensitivity, loan growth in high-yield C&I and CRE, and deposit initiatives moderating betas. Headwinds from competition are manageable with our ALM hedges like SOFR swaps and digital products. We're positioned for stability into 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Lee:
Can you discuss the impact of provision for credit losses drivers?

Michael Chen:
Hi Mike. Our $450 million PCL reflects macro caution on CRE and energy, offset by strong consumer trends. CECL modeling with ML enhancements and climate overlays keeps us conservative at 1.4% coverage. Q4 at 40-50 bps, resilient unless unemployment spikes above 5%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim:
What are your plans for technology investments?

David Kim:
Great question, Sarah. We're doubling down on AI for personalization and fraud—our gen-AI already cuts losses 18%—cloud migrations like AWS/Temenos for scalability, and blockchain for payments. $1.2 billion capex targets 20% efficiency gains, supporting embedded finance and real-time risk models.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Hale for any closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you for your interest in Apex Financial Services. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
